evals.prompt: I'm posting a 1080x1920 talking-head clip to TikTok and Reels. Give me the exact caption style to use: font size in pixels, how many characters per line, how long each caption should stay up, and where on the frame to put them so app buttons don't cover them.
evals.expected_output: Concrete pixel and timing values: a size around 64 to 72 px for sentence captions (or about 140 to 150 px for 1 to 3 word captions), roughly 28 to 32 characters per line, at most 2 lines, at most 17 characters per second, 1 to 6 seconds per cue, and placement inside a centred 900x1400 safe box clear of the bottom app UI.
assertions: Gives a specific font size in pixels between 60 and 150 px and explains which caption style it applies to
Limits captions to at most 2 lines
States a reading speed limit of about 17 characters per second (or an equivalent words-per-minute figure of about 160 to 180)
Places captions inside a cross-platform safe area (a centred box of about 900x1400 or explicit margins that keep text out of roughly the bottom 400 px)
Recommends a dark plate, outline or shadow behind light text for contrast over footage

evals.prompt: Check this caption file before I burn it in and tell me exactly what to fix. It's for a 30 fps vertical video.
evals.expected_output: A cue-by-cue list of problems: cue 1 far too long and fast and needs splitting into several cues; cue 2 is a one-frame flash; cue 3 has three lines and overlaps cue 4; cue 4 stays up too long. Each comes with a concrete fix.
assertions: Identifies that cue 1 is too long or too fast and says to split it into multiple cues rather than shrinking the text
Identifies that cue 2 is on screen far too briefly (well under 1 second)
Identifies that cue 3 has three lines and/or overlaps the start of cue 4
Identifies that cue 4 stays on screen too long (over 6 seconds)

evals.prompt: Write me the ffmpeg command and subtitle file to burn captions onto a 1080x1920 video at about 68 pixel text with a semi-transparent black box behind it, and highlight the word 'week' in orange in the line: I lost four thousand pounds in a single week.
evals.expected_output: An ASS file with PlayResX 1080 and PlayResY 1920 so sizes are pixels, a plate made with BorderStyle 3 using OutlineColour with partial alpha, the highlight applied on a separate text layer above the plate (or otherwise avoiding per-run boxes), a manual line break, and a working ffmpeg subtitles command.
assertions: Sets PlayResX to 1080 and PlayResY to 1920 or otherwise explains how to convert pixel sizes for libass
Uses BorderStyle 3 with the box colour in OutlineColour and a partial alpha value
Avoids putting the colour override on the same line as the plate box, for example by drawing the plate on a separate layer
Breaks the sentence into two lines manually so no line runs off the frame
Provides an ffmpeg command that uses the subtitles filter
